items.summary: Handoff: retain the fleet security evidence matrix and private launch gates. Fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results, so material access, secrets, isolation, release, dependency, monitoring, incident, TLS, and disclosure controls remain unevidenced. Permit only bounded read-only evidence work.

Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but that does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of exploitation. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; allow only bounded reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, provenance, and claims boundaries; continue authorized read-only evidence work only. Do not access credentials or private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Do not treat missing telemetry as a pass or zero.
